confidence.title: Data Confidence & Coverage Transparency
confidence.tracked_high: Tracked zone with direct rover or orbiter instrumentation. Physical parameters come from curated NASA mission datasets.
confidence.tracked_mars_curated: Curated Mars mission zone: surface weather and dust come from Curiosity REMS / Perseverance MEDA telemetry, solar flux from orbital geometry, and terrain/ice constants from published MRO/LOLA references.
confidence.tracked_moon_curated: Curated Moon zone: observation timestamps come from NASA PDS ODE LRO Diviner, diurnal temperatures from Stefan-Boltzmann radiative physics, and terrain/ice constants from published LRO references.
confidence.mars_extrapolated: Honest estimation notice: This coordinate is {{km}} km from {{site}}. Atmospheric telemetry is extrapolated from Curiosity REMS (Gale Crater) + orbital solar geometry, while terrain (slope, roughness, albedo, ice) is estimated by Martian latitude regime.
confidence.moon_pds_partial: Partial orbital coverage: {{count}} real LRO Diviner products were found in NASA PDS ODE for this region, combined with radiative thermal physics. Slope, roughness, and ice are estimated by lunar regime.
confidence.moon_estimated: Honest estimation notice: No direct LRO Diviner products were found in NASA PDS ODE for this exact cell. Surface and terrain parameters are estimated from lunar latitude/longitude regime and Stefan-Boltzmann radiative physics.

mission.earthLimitsMoon: Earth (1g, 1013 mbar, ~2.4 mSv/yr) cannot replicate lunar gravity ({{gravity}} g), hard vacuum ({{pressure}} mbar with electrostatic dust and no convective cooling), or unshielded space radiation ({{radiation}} mSv/yr). Validate these separately in vacuum chambers and flight simulations.

quiz.title: STEAM Mini-Challenge: Test Your Space Intuition
quiz.description: Use the simulators above to verify each answer experimentally.

q1.question: What happens to the mass (kg) and weight (N) of the Perseverance rover (1025 kg) on Mars?
q1.optA: Both its mass and weight drop to 38%
q1.optB: Its mass stays 1025 kg, while its weight in Newtons drops to 38%
q1.optC: Its weight in Newtons stays the same because of its metal wheels
q1.explanation: Correct! Mass is an intrinsic property (1025 kg anywhere), whereas weight depends on local gravity (W = m · g).

q2.question: In a vacuum (no atmosphere), which launch angle gives the maximum horizontal range on any planet?
q2.optA: It depends on the planet's gravity
q2.optB: 75° on the Moon and 30° on Earth
q2.explanation: Without atmospheric drag, sin(2θ) peaks at θ = 45° regardless of the value of g.

q3.question: Compared to Earth, a shallow-water wave in a 5 m deep lunar basin travels...
q3.optA: Slower, because c = √(g · h) and lunar gravity is weaker
q3.optB: Faster, because water weighs less on the Moon
q3.optC: At the exact same speed on both worlds
q3.explanation: Gravity is the restoring force for surface waves: weaker gravity means slower wave propagation (2.85 m/s on the Moon vs. 7.00 m/s on Earth).

atmosphere.title: Air Chemical Composition & Respiratory Habitability (Earth · Mars · Moon)
atmosphere.description: Compare the chemical compounds of each world and how Earth’s gas balance is optimal for human physiology versus life-support (ECLSS / ISRU) challenges on Mars and the Moon.

earth.summary: Ideal balance: 21% O₂ for cellular respiration and 78% N₂ as an inert buffer gas that keeps lung alveoli open and suppresses fire hazards.

mars.summary: Ultra-thin atmosphere with 95.3% CO₂ (lethal hypercapnia) and virtually zero O₂. However, atmospheric CO₂ enables in-situ O₂ production via NASA MOXIE.

moon.summary: No breathable gaseous atmosphere, but ~43% of lunar regolith mass is oxygen bound in metal oxides, plus water ice in polar craters.

roles.n2Earth: Nitrogen: Inert buffer gas maintaining alveolar pressure without toxicity and driving the nitrogen cycle.
roles.o2Earth: Oxygen: Essential electron acceptor for aerobic cellular respiration (ATP).
roles.co2Earth: Carbon dioxide: Triggers breathing reflex at trace levels and maintains mild greenhouse warmth.
roles.co2Mars: Carbon dioxide: Causes immediate hypercapnia in humans, but serves as feedstock for MOXIE O₂ generation.
roles.n2Mars: Nitrogen: Present at 2.7%; must be concentrated to provide habitat buffer gas.
roles.o2CoMars: Trace O₂ (0.13%) and toxic carbon monoxide (CO, 0.08%).
roles.regolithO2: Mineral-bound oxygen in regolith: Extractable by heating Si, Fe, and Ti oxides (>900 °C).
roles.polarIce: Water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters (Shackleton): Ideal for electrolysis.
roles.exosphere: Vestigial exosphere: Sparse atoms that cannot support breathing or sound.

pillars.o2Desc: Below 100 mbar causes cerebral hypoxia and unconsciousness; above 500 mbar causes pulmonary oxygen toxicity and extreme fire risk.
pillars.n2Title: 2. Why Nitrogen Buffer Gas (78% N₂) Is Essential
pillars.n2Desc: Breathing pure oxygen collapses lung alveoli (absorption atelectasis) and turns sparks into infernos. N₂ safely dilutes O₂ and provides total pressure.
pillars.co2Title: 3. Critical CO₂ (< 5 mbar) & Pressure (> 63 mbar) Limits
pillars.co2Desc: Even with enough O₂, >1%–2% CO₂ prevents blood from offloading carbon dioxide. On Mars, CO₂ makes up 95.3% of the gas mix.
